items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the reimbursement of costs to the New York environmental protection and spill compensation fund
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1387

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to the
reimbursement of costs to the New York environmental protection and
spill compensation fund

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to provide for reimbursement to the New
York Environmental Protection and Spill Compensation Fund (the "Oil
Spill Fund") for costs related to cleanup of damage caused by a waste
tire fire and to include the Oil Spill Fund in the Department of Audit
and Control in the listing of those agencies cooperating with the
Department of Environmental Conservation in relation to the Waste Tire
Management and Recycling Act of 2003.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends subdivision 2 of section 27-1903 of the Environmental
Conservation Law to include the Office of the State Comptroller,
Department of Audit and Control, in the listing of agencies the
Department of Environmental Conservation must cooperate and consult
with when implementing waste tire management programs.

Section 2 adds a new subdivision 2 to section 27-1915 of the
Environmental Conservation Law to provide for reimbursement of costs
to the Oil Spill Fund for the following: (a) cleanup of petroleum
contamination resulting from any waste tire fire; (b) any damage claim
paid by the Oil Spill Fund as a result of any waste tire fire; and (c)
all other direct or indirect costs related to the remediation of
petroleum contamination resulting from any waste tire fire.

Section 3 provides for an immediate effective date and is deemed to
have been in effect as of May 15, 2003.

 DISCUSSION :

Pursuant to Navigation Law article 12, the Oil Spill Fund pays for the
cleanup and removal of petroleum spills conducted under the direction
of the Department of Environmental Conservation. As it is estimated
that every tire contains, on the average, three to four gallons of
petroleum, and as the discharge that can result from the burning of
tires is a petroleum product, the fund must pay for the cleanup and
removal of such contamination. Typically, petroleum contamination from
the burning of tires is very costly to remediate, and, in the absence
of a responsible party to reimburse the Oil Spill Fund for the cost of
the cleanup, the fund must write off this expense. This bill will
allow the Oil Spill Fund to recoup its expenditures for cleaning up
any petroleum by-products associated with the burning of tires.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2013-14: A.1684/EnCon
2011-12: A.991/Encon
200910: A.1574/Encon
2007-08: A.3316/Encon
2005-06, A4794/Encon
2004:  A.11474/Passed

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and is deemed to have been in
effect as of May 15, 2003.

summary: Provides for the reimbursement of costs of the New York environmental protection and spill compensation fund in the department of audit and control.
